title: Construction, 1878–1888 CE
description: Frederick William Stevens designed the terminus for the railway era. UNESCO describes a synthesis of Victorian Gothic Revival and Indian building traditions.

title: Inscribed on the World Heritage List
description: The World Heritage Centre records this inscription in its property listing.

title: Completed in 1924 CE
description: The gateway commemorated the 1911 visit of George V and Queen Mary. The Mumbai district account dates its completion to 1924.

title: Royal visit commemorated by the gateway
description: The commemorated royal visit took place thirteen years before the gateway was completed.

title: Opened in 1986 CE
description: Fariborz Sahba designed this Bahá’í House of Worship, inaugurated in 1986. Its lotus form is made from repeated structural petals.

title: Construction, 1650–1656 CE
description: Shah Jahan commissioned the congregational mosque as part of his imperial city. Delhi Tourism places its completion in 1656.

title: Foundation to inauguration, 1921–1931 CE
description: Edwin Lutyens designed the memorial to commemorate soldiers of the Indian Army. Its foundation stone was laid in 1921 and it was inaugurated in 1931.

title: Memorial inaugurated
description: The memorial was inaugurated a decade after its foundation stone was laid.

title: Completed in 1734 CE
description: Sawai Jai Singh II commissioned the observatory in the early eighteenth century. Its architectural instruments were built to observe celestial positions.

title: Inscribed on the World Heritage List
description: The World Heritage Centre records this inscription in its property listing.

title: Major phases, 8th–16th centuries CE
description: Chittorgarh is part of the serial Hill Forts of Rajasthan inscription. Its long history includes successive phases of occupation and major Rajput building campaigns.

title: Inscribed as part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan
description: The World Heritage Centre records this inscription in its property listing.

title: Major fortification, 15th century CE
description: Rana Kumbha is associated with the fifteenth-century fortifications at Kumbhalgarh. Later buildings within the walls belong to other phases.

title: Inscribed as part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan
description: The World Heritage Centre records this inscription in its property listing.

title: Founded in 1459 CE
description: Rao Jodha laid the foundation in 1459. The museum trust records major later phases under Rao Maldeo and Maharaja Ajit Singh.
locator: Early building phases and palace expansion

title: Beginning of Ajit Singh’s reign
description: The trust identifies Ajit Singh’s reign as a major period of palace construction beginning in 1707.
locator: Early building phases and palace expansion

title: 15th century CE
description: The Adinatha temple at Ranakpur belongs to a fifteenth-century Jain building campaign. Rajasthan Tourism identifies its carved marble as a defining feature.

title: Early principal temples, 11th–13th centuries CE
description: Dilwara is a group of Jain temples built in different periods. The Vimal Vasahi and Luna Vasahi are among its earliest and are renowned for intricately carved interiors.

title: Present shrine consecrated in 1951 CE
description: The site has a long history of rebuilding. The current shrine belongs to a twentieth-century reconstruction, consecrated in 1951.

title: Sixteenth-century rebuilding phase
description: Gujarat Tourism distinguishes the religious traditions of Dwarka from phases of rebuilding, especially in the sixteenth and nineteenth centuries.

title: Harappan occupation, c. 3000–1500 BCE
description: Dholavira preserves a long sequence of Harappan occupation. The mapped ruins include multiple divisions of the settlement and its engineered system for water storage.

title: Inscribed on the World Heritage List
description: The World Heritage Centre records this inscription in its property listing.

title: Early 16th century CE
description: The congregational mosque belongs to the Gujarat Sultanate phase of Champaner. The park preserves the mosque alongside the fortified capital and earlier remains.

title: Champaner-Pavagadh inscribed on the World Heritage List
description: The World Heritage Centre records this inscription in its property listing.

title: Construction, 1572–1573 CE
description: Sidi Saiyyed's mosque was built near the close of Gujarat Sultanate rule. The municipal heritage account records its completion in 1573.
locator: Sidi Saiyyed Mosque, architecture and jalis

title: Construction began in 1213 CE
description: The Rudreshwara temple at Palampet was commissioned in the Kakatiya period. UNESCO dates the beginning of its construction to 1213.
locator: Outstanding Universal Value, construction and materials

title: Inscribed on the World Heritage List
description: The World Heritage Centre records this inscription in its property listing.

title: Qutb Shahi phase, 1518–1687 CE
description: Golconda's origins precede Qutb Shahi rule. The dynasty enlarged the fortified capital over the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

title: Golconda falls to Mughal forces
description: The Mughal capture ended the Qutb Shahi period at Golconda.

title: Qutb Shahi burials, 16th–17th centuries CE
description: The funerary complex contains the tombs of the Qutb Shahi dynasty and associated structures. Conservation has worked across the ensemble, including landscape and water features.

title: Heritage park conservation milestone
description: Documents work across tombs, gardens and water infrastructure.

title: Completed in 1035 CE
description: Rajendra I commissioned the temple for his new Chola capital. It is the Gangaikonda Cholapuram component of the Great Living Chola Temples.

title: Added to the Great Living Chola Temples inscription
description: The World Heritage Centre records this inscription in its property listing.

title: Major documented phases, 12th–17th centuries CE
description: The temple grew through multiple periods of patronage. The site dossier describes an extensive living temple town, with phases including Chola, Pandya, Vijayanagara and Nayaka work.

title: Documented phases from the 12th century CE
description: District records describe contributions by rulers from the twelfth century. The celebrated Third Corridor belongs to a later Sethupathi campaign.

title: Early 8th century CE
description: The temple is associated with the Pallava ruler Narasimhavarman II, also called Rajasimha, and later work under Mahendravarman III.

title: Documented patronage in 1517 CE
description: The temple has a long history of patronage. The trust connects a dated donation by Krishnadevaraya in 1517 with the mandapa bearing his name.
locator: Temple History, Krishnadevaraya Mandapam and inner precinct

title: Gilding recorded in an inscription
description: The record is dated 1518 and describes the gilding of the vimana.

title: 16th century CE
description: The Veerabhadra Temple is a Vijayanagara complex linked to the patronage of Virupanna and Viranna. Painted ceilings and sculpted granite are documented features.

title: Principal shrine, 12th century CE
description: The present principal shrine is associated with the Eastern Ganga dynasty. Its construction belongs to the twelfth century and the complex remains in ritual use.

title: Principal phase, 11th century CE
description: The principal fabric of Lingaraj belongs to the eleventh century. The Ekamra Kshetra dossier places it within a wider landscape of shrines and sacred water bodies.

title: Tomar phase, 1398–1516 CE
description: The fort's known history spans much earlier evidence than the Tomar palace phase. The tentative-list dossier identifies extensive work under Man Singh Tomar.

title: 15th century CE, attribution disputed
description: The Dhar district account attributes the palace to Ghiyasuddin Khalji. An architectural survey proposes the earlier reign of Mahmud Khalji I. The date range reflects both attributions.

title: Early 17th century CE
description: Jahangir Mahal is associated with the Bundela ruler Bir Singh Deo. It forms part of the palace ensemble in Orchha's fortified river setting.
locator: Description of palace plans and fort complex

title: Carved lower band, c. 6th century CE
description: The architectural survey dates the carved foliage band on stylistic grounds to approximately the sixth century.

title: Construction, 1784–1791 CE
description: Asaf-ud-Daula commissioned the imambara in 1784. Lucknow district records the building campaign in the context of famine relief.

title: Present principal shrine, 1780 CE
description: The official Kashi portal credits Ahilyabai Holkar with rebuilding the present temple in 1780. The date describes the principal shrine within a larger living sacred precinct.
locator: History of the present temple and its management

title: Temple management transferred to a trust
description: The Uttar Pradesh government took over the temple and entrusted its administration to a trust.
locator: History of the present temple and its management

title: Built c. 1600 CE
description: The Malla ruler Bir Hambir is credited with building the Rasmancha. It served as a ceremonial gathering place for images during the Ras festival.

title: Built c. 1555 CE
description: The Portuguese built the palace around 1555 and presented it to the ruler of Cochin. The Dutch renovated the building in the seventeenth century.

title: Dutch renovation
description: The Dutch renovated the palace after taking control of Cochin in 1663.

title: Rebuilt, 1897–1912 CE
description: The Wadiyar palace was rebuilt after a fire in 1897. Henry Irwin designed the present palace, completed in 1912.
locator: Description of palace and domed towers

title: Palace extension
description: Karnataka Tourism documents an extension added in 1940.

title: 17th-century campaign, c. 1626–1656 CE
description: Gol Gumbaz is the mausoleum of Muhammad Adil Shah of Bijapur. The domed chamber contains the Whispering Gallery around its interior.

title: Construction, 1896–1906 CE
description: The colonial prison was built for cellular confinement and held political prisoners. Only part of its original seven-wing plan survives.
locator: Description, radial plan and National Memorial

title: Dedicated as a national memorial
description: The preserved complex was dedicated as a National Memorial on 11 February 1979.
locator: Description, radial plan and National Memorial

title: 17th century CE
description: The nine-storey palace is linked to the Namgyal ruler Sengge Namgyal. It stands above the old town of Leh.

title: Founded in 1680–1681 CE
description: Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso founded the monastery in the late seventeenth century. It remains a working Buddhist institution.
locator: Tawang Monastery, history and assembly hall

title: Nineteenth-century rebuilding phase
description: Gujarat Tourism distinguishes the religious traditions of Dwarka from phases of rebuilding, especially in the sixteenth and nineteenth centuries.
